operations.description: Turn a feature flag on or off in one environment. This is a live production change: every SDK instance currently evaluating this flag in this environment — web, mobile and backend alike — switches to the other branch as soon as this call returns, for every real user it serves. It is reversible by toggling back, but it is not a private or staged edit

params.description: The project's own key, from launchdarkly-project-list's `key` field
params.name: project_key

params.description: The flag's own key, from launchdarkly-flag-list's `key` field
params.name: feature_flag_key

schema.description: A JSON Patch (RFC 6902) document with exactly one operation, setting a single environment's on/off state: `[{"op": "replace", "path": "/environments/<environment_key>/on", "value": true}]` turns the flag on in that environment, `"value": false` turns it off. `<environment_key>` is that environment's own key (from launchdarkly-environment-list's `key` field), written literally into the JSON Pointer string — it is not a request parameter LaunchDarkly could confuse with a URL segment

op.description: This connector's curated toggle uses only `replace`; LaunchDarkly's PATCH also accepts `add`, `remove` and `test`, none of which this connector exposes

path.description: A JSON Pointer to one environment's `on` bit: `/environments/{environment_key}/on`

value.description: `true` turns the flag on in that environment, `false` turns it off

operations.repeatability_condition: the body schema admits exactly one JSON Patch `replace` onto one environment's `on` bit (maxItems 1, op pinned to `replace`, path pinned to `/environments/{key}/on`), so it sets an absolute value and never a toggle or a delta — re-sending it lands the flag where the caller asked, however many times it runs

environments.description: The flag's environments after the patch was applied, in the same shape launchdarkly-flag-get returns — read the affected environment's `on` field back to confirm the toggle took effect
